tiers.text: Only one front door. Enough people inside to make getaways awkward and conflict dangerous.

variants.text: The yard door's hinge pins are on the outside, and the pavement cellar flap is rotten along one edge. You can place the vein to the yard: under the back room, against the far wall.

tiers.text: Through the one door you can see people moving, and some narrow shelves. Feels a bit claustrophobic.

variants.text: The yard door round the back is old, and the cellar flap in the pavement has seen better decades.

physics.miss: There's a door. A flickering light in the store. Oh, and shelves. Yup, it's a shop.

tiers.text: There's someone chatting to the shopkeeper, and a few other customers browsing. Seems like more people in the back, too.
You can make out at least 2 people by the till, and likely more elsewhere in the shop.

life.miss: At first you think it's empty. Then you notice the customers. And the staff. Yup, those are people alright.

tiers.text: There's a sense of passiveness, being resigned to your fate. Boredom and complacency is what you pick up on, not vigilance or danger.
They say the active displaces the passive. This place should have been displaced a long time ago.

emotion.miss: Tired faces under strip lights. Almost everyone here would rather be somewhere else. Nothing you can use.

tiers.text: Stock comes in round the back, and sometimes deliveries go in via the pavement flap. He's due soon, and often leaves the flap open between crates.

variants.text: The drayman comes on the hour and props the pavement flap open between crates. The camera over the till pans on a slow loop, and you can count it.

tiers.text: Stock comes in round the back on some kind of schedule. The back room gets busy, then quiet, then busy again.

time.miss: People come and go. You can't make a pattern of it.

tiers.text: It's a bad night for this shop's luck. The card machine has gone down twice already, and it's due again.

variants.text: The camera over the till is aimed at the queue, not the staff door. There's a stripe of floor beside the counter it has never once seen. And the card machine is due to go down again.

tiers.text: Small things keep going wrong in this shop. The door chime sticks, and the card machine sulks.

variants.text: The CCTV over the till isn't quite right. It's something about where it's pointing.

fate.miss: You're feeling lucky tonight. Then you notice that you stepped in dog poo, and change your mind.

tiers.text: The yard door's hinge pins are on the outside. Stiff, but removable, with enough elbow grease.
The yard door round the back is old: soft paint, a warped frame, and a lock newer than the wood.

physics.miss: The door looks too solid for you to kick in.

tiers.text: One woman on the till, a regular at the counter who won't stop talking. In the back, men in shop fleeces stock shelves; more men than the shelves need.
A regular chats with (or rather, at) the woman at the till. A few people stock shelves near the back.

life.miss: Two people near the till. You hear someone else, but can't tell if they're behind the shelves or further back in the shop.

tiers.text: The woman on the till would accept any story that means she doesn't have to deal with hassle. The men in the back are bored, and boredom makes people easy to talk past.
The woman on the till hates this job with the intensity that makes you just not care anymore.

emotion.miss: Tired faces under strip lights. Almost everyone here would rather be somewhere else. Nothing you can use.

tiers.text: The regular scratches each card on the counter and talks her through it. While he talks, she nods and looks at nothing else. He has never won more than two quid, and has never once stopped talking.
One on the till, and a regular at the counter who's going nowhere. She keeps half an eye on him.

life.miss: A queue, a till, someone behind it. People come and go.

tiers.text: She's forty minutes from the end of her shift and won't spend any of them on an argument. Anyone who asks her for anything gets waved at whatever's nearest.
She wants this shift over more than she wants anything in the shop.

emotion.miss: Her face is set to 'next, please'. Nothing gets past it.

tiers.text: The card machine has tape round its middle and drops a payment every few customers. She's stopped apologising for it.
The queue moves in fits. Every so often the whole shop waits on something at the till.

fate.miss: Nothing at the till looks broken, as far as you can see.

tiers.text: The shelving runs floor to ceiling down one wall and stands a foot off it. Behind the roll cages there's a strip of floor nobody walks.
Tall shelving, roll cages, a lot of cardboard. You can't see from one end to the other.

physics.miss: Shelves and cages, with stock on all of them.

tiers.text: Two men in shop fleeces are on the restock. One of them is doing it. The other is holding a single box of teabags, and has been for some time.
More men in fleeces back here than the shelves need. Not all of them are stocking.

life.miss: Someone's back there. You hear a box land, then nothing.

tiers.text: Stock comes off the van in runs. Between runs the aisle stands empty long enough to boil a kettle.
Stock comes through in batches. Sometimes the aisle is busy, sometimes it isn't.

time.miss: Boxes come in, boxes go out. You couldn't say when.

tiers.text: The lock is newer than the door, and cheap. The price sticker is still on the face: £8.99.
The lock is newer than the door. Somebody spent money back here, though not much.

physics.miss: A door, a lock, a handle. Nothing more from here.

tiers.text: There's a crate-shaped scuff on the frame at hip height. Whoever takes the deliveries down goes with his hands full, and doesn't always come back to lock up.
The handle's worn bright. This door gets more use than a cellar door needs.

fate.miss: Nothing about the door is lucky or unlucky. It's shut.

tiers.text: He's on a dating app, swiping left with great care. He looks up whenever the yard door creaks, and at nothing else.
One man, a shop fleece, a phone. He's facing the yard door, not the gate.

life.miss: Someone's in the yard. You smell the smoke before you see him.

tiers.text: He lit this one as you came round the corner. He smokes them down to the filter, one per break, unless the shift's got to him.
He's not long started. His breaks run a cigarette each.

time.miss: He's on a break. You can't tell how long he's had, or how long he's got.

tiers.text: The hinge pins are on the outside, and the paint over the tops of them has cracked. They've been out before, and the door painted back on after.
The door is old: soft paint, a warped frame, and a lock newer than the wood.

physics.miss: Old wood under a lot of paint. You can't tell which is holding the other up.

tiers.text: The paint round the latch is worn to the wood. He goes in and out all shift, and between smokes the door sits on the latch, not the lock.
The paint round the latch is worn to the wood. This door opens a lot.

time.miss: Yup, it's a door, and it has been opened at some point in the last century. You think.

tiers.text: The drayman comes on the hour. He props both doors back and leaves them up while he fetches the next barrel from the van, which is parked on the zigzags.
Deliveries go down the chute. The drayman's due, roughly.

time.miss: Two doors in the pavement. You can't say when they last opened.

tiers.text: The left door's hinge has rusted to a flake. The crate on top is what's keeping it shut.
The iron edges are sound. The wood between them has gone soft.

physics.miss: Iron edges, old wood, shut. Nothing more from up here.

tiers.text: Everyone at the bus stop is watching the road for the bus, or their phone for the bus. Nobody's looking down.
The bus stop's full. They're all facing the road.

life.miss: People going past, too many to read any one of them.

tiers.text: He's scrolling with the sound off. Now and then he glances at the vein, the way you'd pat a pocket to check your keys are still there.
One man in a shop fleece, on a crate, half turned from the ladder.

life.miss: Someone's down there. You hear the crate creak before you see him.

tiers.text: Every few minutes, near enough on the dot, he turns on the crate to look at the vein, and stays turned while he reads whatever's come in on his phone.
He shifts round on the crate every few minutes. He hasn't got comfortable yet.

time.miss: He's been down there a while. You can't tell how long, or how long he's got left.

tiers.text: He's bored past caring. He has read the label on every box down here, and started on the barrels.
He's bored, and has been since he sat down.

emotion.miss: You can't read his face from the ladder.

cards.label: {today} — The approach
cards.text: A late-opening shop, still trading: strip lights, a queue of two, a bus stop outside. The vein is in the cellar, under the back room. There will be guards nearby; everyone else in there is a witness. Get this wrong and you get it wrong in front of a whole street.
You can make out 2 ways in. One: front door, past the till and staff door, then stockroom and stairs. Two: round the back, yard, door, stockroom, stairs. One is easier, but you're much more exposed.

choices.label: Walk in as a customer
choices.result_text: You go in the front, like anyone wanting milk at this hour.

choices.label: Round the back
choices.result_text: You walk past the shop and turn down the side passage, away from the lights.

cards.text: What you read buys you other ways in. Some skip the shop altogether.

choices.label: The cellar flap
choices.result_text: You stay out front, on the pavement, by the flap that drops straight into the cellar.

success.result_text: The street folds. You step out in the cellar with the vein under your feet and the shop still trading over your head.

fail.result_text: The fold drops you in the cellar, and into a stack of bottles. Upstairs, somebody stops talking.

cards.text: The door chimes. Three aisles, a humming fridge, a regular at the counter in no hurry to leave. The staff door is behind the till.
Nobody's guarding the stockroom. But staff come back here for stock every few minutes, and a stranger among the shelves takes some explaining. The cellar door is at the far end.

success.result_text: You wait for the lull between restocks and cross the stockroom in it.

fail.result_text: The lull is shorter than you thought. You're halfway across when someone comes through with a box.

choices.label: Keep to the blind side of the shelving

success.result_text: You keep a cage of stock between you and the doorway all the way to the cellar door.

fail.result_text: You come round the end of the shelving into someone coming the other way.

success.result_text: Nobody's restocking. Judging by the shelves, nobody has in a while.

fail.result_text: Somebody is, and they're behind the next cage.

cards.text: Or let something you brought do the work.

choices.label: Prophet's Breath: know where they are
choices.result_text: You know where everyone in the building will be for the next minute. None of them will be here.

cards.text: The cellar door is locked, and the lock is newer than the door. Somebody spent money back here, and not on the shop.

success.result_text: The lock turns over. You ease the door open on a flight of stone steps and go down.

fail.result_text: The lock opens, but the pick slips first and the door rattles in its frame. Behind you, someone says "Oi."

success.result_text: Somebody left it on the latch for a delivery and forgot. You go down.

fail.result_text: It's locked, but the frame is soft. It gives when you lean on it, and not quietly.

cards.text: Or make some noise, and hope the shop makes more.

choices.label: Walk down
choices.result_text: No lock, just a hook and eye. You lift the hook and go down.

success.result_text: You put your shoulder into it. The frame splits and the door opens on the cellar steps.

cover.text: Out front, the fridges hum and the radio keeps playing. Nobody comes to look.

fail.result_text: It gives on the third go, with a crack like a dropped crate. Everyone in the building heard that.

choices.label: Blast the door

cover.text: Out front, the fridges hum and the radio keeps playing. Nobody comes to look.

choices.result_text: The door comes off and goes down the stairs ahead of you.

cards.text: Round the back: bins, flattened boxes, a stack of empty crates. A man in a shop fleece is having a smoke beside the yard door, which is the door you need. He's watching the door more than his phone.

choices.label: Wait for the smoker to finish

success.result_text: He grinds the cigarette out, checks his phone and goes back inside. The yard is yours, and so is the door.

fail.result_text: He lights another off the first one and turns round to do it. He's looking right at you.

success.result_text: You lift a crate off the stack and walk to the door like you're paid by the drop. He nods at the crate and goes back to his phone.

fail.result_text: He asks where the van is. You say it's parked on the road. He asks how the pallet got here then. Your suggestion of "magic?" doesn't persuade him.

cards.text: Or trust to luck, or to something you brought.

success.result_text: He has. There's a cigarette end still smoking by the bins and nobody standing over it.

fail.result_text: He hasn't. He's only round the corner, and now he's round it facing you.

choices.label: Prophet's Breath: know when he goes in
choices.result_text: You know the second he'll turn to go in. You're behind the bins when he does, and at the door when it shuts.

choices.label: Time Pearl: freeze him
choices.result_text: He stops with the lighter halfway to his mouth. You walk past him to the door. From his perspective you're just a trick of the light, there and gone in an instant.

cards.text: The yard door: old wood, painted so many times the gaps have filled in. It's locked from the inside. The stockroom is through it, and the cellar door beyond that.

success.result_text: The pins come out with some persuasion and the door lifts off its hinges. You lean it against the wall and step into the stockroom.

fail.result_text: The second pin sticks, then comes out all at once and rings off the step. The door's open, and someone inside heard it.

success.result_text: The lock's newer than the door and not as good as it looks. It turns, and you're in the stockroom.

fail.result_text: The lock turns in the end, but the pick skids first and the whole door rattles. Someone inside heard that.

cards.text: Or make some noise about it.

choices.label: Walk in
choices.result_text: It isn't locked, only stuck. One shove and you're in the stockroom.

success.result_text: Paint and old wood. It gives on the second shove.

cover.text: Out front, the fridges hum and the radio keeps playing. Nobody comes to look.

fail.result_text: It gives on the third, all at once, and slams loudly into a cage of crisps. Someone probably heard that, and now your shoulder hurts.

choices.label: Blast the door

cover.text: Out front, the fridges hum and the radio keeps playing. Nobody comes to look.

choices.result_text: What was left of the door lands in the stockroom ahead of you. Loudly.

cards.text: The cellar flap: two iron-edged doors in the pavement, where deliveries go down the chute. It's the shortest way in. No till, no stockroom, no stairs. It's also on a busy street, in full view of the bus stop.

choices.label: Take the flap while the drayman has it open
choices.result_text: The drayman props the flap open and goes back to his van for the next crate. You go down the chute before he's back.

success.result_text: The rotten edge gives under the bar with a soft crunch. You lift the flap, drop through and let it down over your head.

fail.result_text: The rotten edge goes all at once and the flap bangs on the pavement. You're through, but not unseen.

choices.label: Hope no one on the street looks down

success.result_text: Londoners don't look at the pavement. You're down the chute before anyone does.

fail.result_text: You're halfway down the chute when someone on the pavement stops walking.

cards.text: Or the quick way, which is also the loud way, on a street full of people.

choices.label: Blast the flap

cover.text: A bus pulls away from the stop at the same moment and takes the noise with it.

choices.result_text: The flap goes up in two pieces and comes down in more. You're down the hole before the street has finished turning round.

cards.text: You land among barrels and boxes in the cellar. The till, the stockroom and the stairs are all over your head. Between you and the vein is one guard on a crate, half turned away from you.

choices.label: Wait for the guard on the vein to turn

success.result_text: He turns to read a message on his phone. You're across the cellar before he's finished it.

fail.result_text: He turns, but the wrong way. He sees you crouching silently. Somehow you don't think he'd believe you if you said you were looking for a lost contact lens.

success.result_text: He gets up with a yawn, stretching his arms out. He gives you a nod as you walk past confidently.

fail.result_text: He hears your steps, looks up, and scrambles to his feet in a panic. So much for the quiet approach.

choices.label: Prophet's Breath: know when he turns
choices.result_text: You know which second he'll look at his phone. You move in that second.

cards.text: Or stop him where he sits.

choices.label: Time Pearl: freeze him
choices.result_text: He stops mid-yawn. You quickly walk round him to the vein. From his perspective you're just a shadow moving at the edge of his vision, gone before he can even glance in your direction.

cards.text: A woman at the bus stop has stopped scrolling. She's watching you, and so is her phone.
Someone's seen you who isn't paid to stop you. They can't fight you, and you can't fight them. But they can tell someone, and on a street like this, someone is always listening.

success.result_text: You give them a reason boring enough to believe. They decide you're not their problem and go back to their evening.

fail.result_text: They don't buy it. They're already dialling, and they're not dialling a friend.

success.result_text: You step out of their line of sight and stay out of it until they decide they imagined you.

fail.result_text: They follow you with their eyes, then with their phone.

cards.text: The smoker looks up, and keeps looking.
A man in a shop fleece is looking at you across the yard. He isn't surprised. He's turned sideways, one arm behind him, holding a phone or a weapon. He's watching you.

choices.label: Take him down
choices.result_text: You go for him before he's finished deciding.

success.result_text: You tell him you're with the landlord. The details matter less than how bored you sound. He puts the phone away.

fail.result_text: He's heard that one before. He shouts for the others.

success.result_text: You get behind the bins and wait. He looks for a while, then decides he imagined you.

fail.result_text: He doesn't look away. He walks towards the bins, shouting.

cards.text: Something you brought, or the road home.

choices.label: Pan's Rapture
choices.result_text: He forgets about you, and about his phone, and stands smiling at the bins.

choices.label: Blast him
choices.result_text: One bang in a small yard. He goes down, and the windows along the back of the street light up.

cards.text: A man in the stockroom has seen you. He puts his box down carefully, like he'll need both hands.

choices.label: Take him down
choices.result_text: You close the distance before he's straightened up.

success.result_text: You tell him the manager sent you back for bags. He's never met the manager either. He lets it go.

fail.result_text: He doesn't buy it. He calls through to the others.

success.result_text: You're behind the cages before he's straightened up. He stares at the gap where you were, then picks up his box.

fail.result_text: He sees where you went, and calls through to the others.

cards.text: Something you brought, or the road home.

choices.label: Pan's Rapture
choices.result_text: He sits down on a pallet of water, smiling, and forgets why he stood up. He starts humming the Venga Bus song.

choices.label: Blast him
choices.result_text: One bang among the shelving. He goes down, and so does a cage of crisps.

cards.text: The yard door opens from inside. A man in a shop fleece looks out at you.
A door bangs, and a man in a shop fleece comes round the shelving with a box in his arms. He isn't staff. Staff don't look at you like that.
The shop's awake. Daniela is on the phone, customers are leaving without their shopping, and the men in fleeces are searching the building. If they find you now, they find you in front of everyone.

success.result_text: You fold yourself in behind a stack of crates. They walk past twice and don't look down.

fail.result_text: They find you behind the crates.

success.result_text: You point at the yard door and say he went that way. They half believe you, and half is enough.

fail.result_text: They know every face that belongs in this shop, and yours isn't one of them.

choices.label: Pan's Rapture
choices.result_text: The search goes soft. The men in fleeces stand about in the aisle, smiling at the crisps.

cards.text: Or scare them off, or leave while you still can.

choices.label: Panic

cover.text: They go without a word, and the shop barely notices.

choices.result_text: Two of them go white and run out through the yard door.

cards.text: The stockroom isn't empty. Men in shop fleeces are stacking a shelf that's already full. They work for whoever owns the cellar, not the shop, and they're between you and the cellar door.

choices.label: Fight
choices.result_text: They stop pretending to stack shelves.

success.result_text: You tell them you've been sent down to check the cellar. Nobody wants to be the one who stopped the wrong person. They let you by.

fail.result_text: One of them asks who sent you. There's no good answer, and his box goes down on the floor.

cards.text: Something you brought.

choices.label: Prophet's Breath: skip the post
choices.result_text: You know where each of them will be in the next ten seconds, and you're never there.

choices.label: Time Pearl: freeze and rush past
choices.result_text: The stockroom stops: a man mid-lift, a box in mid-air. You walk through it and reach the cellar door breathing hard.

choices.label: Time Pearl: freeze the line guard
choices.result_text: The one nearest the cellar door stops mid-sentence. The others don't.

cards.text: Something that makes a post forget what it's for.

choices.label: Pandemonium
choices.result_text: A word in the wrong ear, and they turn on each other, shouting about whose fault you are.

choices.label: Panic

cover.text: They go without a word, and the shop barely notices.

choices.result_text: Two of them go white and leave through the yard door without their coats.

choices.label: Pan's Rapture
choices.result_text: They go soft around the eyes and sit down on the stock. One of them offers you a crisp.

cards.text: The shop door chimes, and keeps chiming. More of the owner's people are coming in the front, past the customers going out.

Over the till, a camera on a bracket pans slowly across the queue. There's a screen in the back somewhere. If it gets a good look at you heading for the staff door, someone will come out to see who you are.

success.result_text: You count the pan and move on the turn. When it comes back, you're a customer looking at crisps.

fail.result_text: The camera turns back early and stops on you. On a screen somewhere in the back, you're the only thing moving.

success.result_text: There's a stripe of floor beside the counter it never sees. You stay on it.

fail.result_text: The stripe is narrower than you thought. Your shoulder's on camera, and the rest of you follows.

success.result_text: The lens flickers and the red light goes out, just long enough. Nobody's fixed it because nobody's noticed.

fail.result_text: It isn't on the blink. The red light stays on, and so does the recording.

cards.text: A camera is a system. It can't be talked round. It can only be stopped.

choices.label: Time Pearl: freeze it
choices.result_text: The camera stops mid-pan. You walk under it, and it starts again on an empty queue.

choices.label: Blast it

cover.text: Out front, a lorry goes by at the same moment. People look at the road, not the ceiling.

choices.result_text: The camera comes off its bracket in pieces. The queue ducks.

cards.text: The camera's had a good look at you. Somebody in the back is watching the screen by now, and they're coming out to look in person.

choices.label: Take him down
choices.result_text: He comes through the staff door expecting a shoplifter. You're ready for him.

success.result_text: By the time he's out, you're behind the fridges. He looks along the aisles and goes back to his screen.

fail.result_text: He's out quicker than you expected and walks straight to where you're standing.

choices.label: Blast him
choices.result_text: One bang by the till. He goes down, and the queue goes out the door.

cards.text: There's a ward on the cellar stairs. The air on the top step feels held, like a breath. Walk through it as you are and it goes off, and whoever set it will know.

choices.label: Step through
choices.result_text: You step through. The air rings once, like a struck glass, and upstairs the radio goes quiet.

success.result_text: You find the thin place in it and go through sideways.

fail.result_text: Halfway through, it notices you. The air rings.

success.result_text: You roll a tin of beans down the steps. The ward takes it. You wait out the ringing, then follow.

fail.result_text: The ward lets the tin roll past and waits for you.

cards.text: Something you brought, or someone else to go first.

success.result_text: You tell a guard you heard something on the stairs. He goes to look and the ward takes him. You step round him.

fail.result_text: He isn't going down those stairs first, not for you. The ward gets you instead.

choices.label: Powder past it
choices.result_text: You go through it as fast as the powder will take you.

success.result_text: You fold the stairs and step out at the bottom. The ward is behind you, guarding nothing.

fail.result_text: The fold lands short, right on the top step.

cards.text: A ward is a system. Systems can be stopped.

choices.label: Time Pearl: freeze the ward
choices.result_text: The ward stops mid-breath. You walk through it before it starts again.

cards.text: The woman on the till is scanning a meal deal without looking at it. Her badge says DANIELA. The staff door is beside her, propped open on a box of receipts. To get through it, you need her to be looking somewhere else, or not caring.

success.result_text: "Through the back, on the left. Don't touch anything." You don't plan to touch anything on the left.

fail.result_text: "No public toilet." She says it to your back, because you're already through the staff door. Now she's watching it.

choices.label: Spin her the story she wants

success.result_text: You say you're here about the boiler. She's already pointing at the back. Nobody wants to be the one who knows about the boiler.

fail.result_text: She asks which company sent you. You name one. She writes it down, then watches you go through the door.

choices.label: Wait until she's serving the regular

success.result_text: The regular starts on his scratchcards, one at a time, with commentary. Daniela can't get away from him. You walk through the staff door.

fail.result_text: The regular wins two quid and goes quiet to enjoy it. In the silence, Daniela looks up at you with your hand on the staff door.

cards.text: The staff door is still propped open, and Daniela is still beside it.

choices.label: Hope the card machine goes down

success.result_text: The card machine says CONNECTING and keeps saying it. The queue turns on Daniela, and nobody's watching the door.

fail.result_text: The card machine works first time, for once. Daniela looks up, pleased, straight at you.

choices.label: Prophet's Breath: know when she's busy
choices.result_text: You know the exact second she'll turn to the cigarette cabinet. When she does, you're already through the staff door.

cards.text: Daniela looks up from the till, straight at you. Her hand goes under the counter, to the phone.
The street's right there. You can leave now and hope no one noticed you; if they did, they'll be on guard next time.

choices.label: Walk out calmly
choices.result_text: You leave like a customer who couldn't find what they wanted.

success.result_text: You go out the quickest way and keep going. You get some glances from passersby, but more like you're someone running for a bus than a would-be raider.

fail.result_text: They cut you off. Nowhere to run now.

success.result_text: The fold sets you down on a pavement a street away, next to a bin. A cat eyes you disdainfully, then goes back to licking itself.

fail.result_text: The fold lands short, in the middle of the shop floor, in front of everyone. You briefly consider trying to convince them you're David Blaine and this is a trick. Briefly.

cards.text: You give it a count of ten, and listen.
Then you get on with it.
The cellar: one bulb, old brick, barrels, and a vein humming in the floor you can feel through your shoes. Oh, and the guards now looking at you.

choices.label: Fight for the room
choices.result_text: They don't give it up.

choices.label: Walk to the vein
choices.result_text: Nobody's posted down here. You walk across to the vein.

success.result_text: You say you've been sent to take a reading. They've been down here long enough to want it to be true. They go back to chatting about last night's game.

fail.result_text: One of them asks who sent you. You panic and say Mr. Bean. One of them raises an eyebrow, the other smiles. Both square up to you.

choices.label: Prophet's Breath: slip past
choices.result_text: You know when and where each of them will look. It's almost too easy to make sure they don't see you.

cards.text: You kneel on the vein. It's warm, like a pipe. Over your head, you hear the shop door chime faintly.
This is what you came for. Claim it and it's yours, and the people who had it will know who took it. Loot it and you leave with what you can carry. If nobody saw you, nobody knows.

choices.label: Claim it
choices.result_text: You take it outright. Word gets round fast - it always does - and your relationship with whoever ran this patch takes a hit.

choices.label: Loot and leave
choices.result_text: You take what you can carry and leave the rest where it stands. The vein doesn't feel quite as warm as when you came in.

cards.text: Upstairs, the shop door chimes and keeps chiming: the owner's people, coming in past the customers going out. They'll be on the cellar stairs in a minute.

choices.label: Reach for the vein
choices.result_text: You reach for it anyway, with feet on the stairs.

cards.text: Upstairs, the shop has stopped pretending. Claim it and it's yours, and the people who had it will know who took it. Loot it and at least you'll be carrying something when you run.

choices.label: Claim it
choices.result_text: You take it outright. Word gets round fast — it always does — and the relationship with whoever ran this patch takes the hit that comes with being seen to do it.

choices.label: Loot and leave
choices.result_text: You take what you can carry and leave the rest where it stands. Someone else's problem, still.

cards.text: The way you came is full of people looking for you. There's the yard, if you're quick. There's the shop floor, where a customer is just a customer.

success.result_text: Out the yard door, over the bins, down the side passage. Nobody catches you.

fail.result_text: They're waiting in the yard.

success.result_text: You come up through the stockroom and out past the till. Daniela sees you, then looks at the clock instead. Eleven minutes till the end of her shift.

fail.result_text: Halfway down the aisle, a man in a shop fleece steps out from behind the crisps and blocks the door.

success.result_text: The fold takes you out of the cellar and sets you down two streets away.

fail.result_text: The fold lands short, at the top of the cellar stairs.

cards.text: You're in the stockroom, and the yard door behind you is open to the night. The silence you hear is either completely normal, or the sound of alerted guards listening. Your paranoia makes it heard to know which.
The stockroom: cages of crisps, a pallet of water, a mop in a bucket. The cellar door is at the far end.
The cellar door is behind a stack of empty crates. Warm air comes through the gap underneath it, and a hum you can feel in the floor. That's the vein.
Outside, the bus stop queue hasn't moved and nobody's looking at you. The vein is still under the shop. It'll be there next time, and so will they.
